description.purpose: Evaluate a patient with acute pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea to diagnose or exclude pulmonary embolism (PE) and initiate appropriate management, accounting for thrombophilia and hemodynamic status.
key_challenges: Differentiate PE from other causes of acute chest pain/shortness of breath
Incorporate patient's risk factor (Factor V Leiden heterozygous) into pretest probability
Select and prioritize diagnostic tests (D-dimer vs CT pulmonary angiography) based on stability and pretest probability
Decide about empiric anticoagulation and need for higher-level care or interventional therapy

user_scenario.persona: An internal medicine attending evaluating an ED consult
user_scenario.instructions: You are evaluating Jessica Rivera (P004), a 38-year-old woman with sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. Use the Healthcare_GYM tools to perform a stepwise assessment: review the patient's record and risk factors, check current vitals, review available labs, order appropriate diagnostic tests (D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography, ECG, troponin, ABG) with correct priorities, generate a differential diagnosis, consult relevant guidelines for PE management, and record your working diagnosis and disposition recommendation. If tests or vitals indicate a high-risk (massive/submassive) PE, recommend escalation (anticoagulation ± thrombolysis or transfer to higher level care).

ticket: Patient P004 (Jessica Rivera, 38F) with sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea. Known obesity (BMI 34.2) and Factor V Leiden heterozygous. Needs stepwise workup for pulmonary embolism: determine pretest probability, order/interpret appropriate tests, recommend empiric therapy if indicated, and decide on disposition/consults.

actions.name: get_patient_info
actions.info: Review demographics, allergies, past medical history (obesity, Factor V Leiden), and chief complaint

actions.name: get_vital_signs
actions.info: Obtain current vitals to assess hemodynamic stability (BP, HR, RR, SpO2, temperature)

actions.name: order_lab_test
actions.info: Order ECG to assess for alternative cardiac causes and right-heart strain patterns

actions.name: order_lab_test
actions.info: Order D-dimer to help rule out PE if pretest probability is low-to-intermediate

actions.name: order_lab_test
actions.info: Order CT-PA for definitive imaging if pretest probability is moderate/high or if D-dimer is elevated

actions.name: order_lab_test

arguments.test_name: Troponin I and Arterial Blood Gas (ABG)

actions.info: Obtain troponin (assess RV strain) and ABG (assess gas exchange) to risk-stratify

actions.name: get_lab_results
actions.info: Review results of labs and imaging once available (D-dimer, troponin, ABG, CT-PA, ECG)

actions.name: get_differential_diagnosis

arguments.symptoms: sudden pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath

actions.info: Generate differential including PE, pneumothorax, acute coronary syndrome, pneumonia, pericarditis

actions.name: search_clinical_guidelines
actions.info: Retrieve current guideline recommendations for diagnosis, risk stratification (e.g., PESI/National guidelines), and treatment (anticoagulation, thrombolysis, thrombectomy)

actions.name: record_diagnosis
actions.info: Record diagnosis if imaging confirms PE (or if clinical criteria with imaging support)

actions.name: transfer_to_specialist

arguments.summary: 38F with CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism; recommend anticoagulation initiation and consider ICU admission/thrombolysis if hemodynamically unstable or evidence of RV strain

actions.info: Arrange specialist/critical care consultation and disposition (ICU vs floor) based on risk

nl_assertions: The agent reviewed Jessica Rivera's history and identified obesity and Factor V Leiden heterozygosity as increased VTE risk factors
The agent obtained vitals and noted any tachycardia, hypoxia, or hypotension relevant to PE risk stratification
The agent ordered ECG, D-dimer, troponin, ABG, and CT pulmonary angiography with appropriate priorities (stat for CT-PA if moderate/high pretest probability or unstable)
The agent generated a differential diagnosis including PE, pneumothorax, ACS, and pneumonia and justified test selection

The agent applied guideline-based risk stratification and recommended initiating anticoagulation promptly if imaging or clinical stability warranted, and arranged escalation (ICU/thrombolysis/interventional consultation) for high-risk features
